  "draft": "[DATE]

[LANDLORD NAME]
[LANDLORD ADDRESS]

Subject: Formal Dispute of Security Deposit Deductions — Nakatia 1bhk

Dear [LANDLORD NAME],

This letter serves as a formal demand for the full refund of my security deposit in the amount of ₹10,000, paid in relation to the residential tenancy at Nakatia 1bhk (hereinafter, "the Property"). My tenancy has concluded.

Upon the termination of the tenancy and my vacation of the Property, I ensured that it was left in a clean, well-maintained condition, consistent with the state at the commencement of the tenancy, accounting for normal wear and tear. The Lease Agreement clearly stipulates the purpose of the security deposit: to cover any damages to the Property beyond normal wear and tear or any outstanding rental dues. I confirm that all rental obligations, including the payment of rent and utilities, were settled in full prior to my departure. Furthermore, I assert that no damage beyond ordinary wear and tear occurred during my occupancy, and therefore, no legitimate basis exists for any deductions from the security deposit.

To date, I have not received an itemized statement of deductions from the security deposit, as is customary and legally required in many jurisdictions, nor have any valid justifications for withholding any portion of the deposit been provided. In the absence of such a transparent and evidence-backed statement, or if any proposed deductions are not demonstrably supported by the specific terms of our Lease Agreement and verifiable evidence of actual damage beyond normal wear and tear, the entire security deposit of ₹10,000 is due for immediate refund. The burden of proof for any deductions rests solely with the landlord.

It is a fundamental principle of tenancy law in India that security deposits must be returned promptly after the termination of a lease, typically within a stipulated period, unless specific, justifiable, and itemized deductions are made for actual damages or unpaid rent, supported by clear and compelling evidence. Without such explicit justification and supporting documentation, the retention of the deposit constitutes an unlawful withholding of funds rightfully belonging to the tenant. This practice is contrary to the spirit and letter of residential tenancy regulations.

Therefore, I formally request the full refund of my security deposit, amounting to ₹10,000, to be remitted to me without further delay.

I expect to receive the full refund within seven (7) days from the date of this letter. Failure to provide the full refund or a detailed, evidence-backed justification for any proposed deductions within this stipulated timeframe will leave me with no option but to escalate this matter. Such escalation may include, but is not limited to, filing a formal complaint with the appropriate consumer forum or rent authority, seeking recovery of the deposit along with any applicable compensation, interest, or penalties as per relevant Indian tenancy laws. I trust that you will take the necessary steps to resolve this matter amicably and promptly.

DepositBack helps organise evidence and draft communication. It does not provide legal representation and does not guarantee any outcome.

Sincerely,

[TENANT NAME]
[TENANT CONTACT INFORMATION]",
